speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are here for a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to understand what's happening, have you ever smoked or been exposed to significant dust or chemical fumes?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an incredibly long duration for these symptoms, and the specific description of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum is very telling. Given your history of recurrent "bronchitis" despite not smoking, have you noticed if your symptoms improve significantly when you take a hot shower or use a steam inhaler?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The combination of a chronic productive cough lasting over 10 years, copious purulent sputum, and recurrent infections in a non-smoker is classic for bronchiectasis. Please review the attached CT Chest images to confirm the diagnosis.
